en: Summary verse: (Matsumura 186) *uddānam*.
For indeed, by one from Sāketa, something was transmitted and then suppressed over time;
a person [forgot] twenty *mātṛkāpadas* of what was not yet done, [but remembered] twelve of what was to be done.
(Matsumura 187)
Having entered the rainy season retreat at Sāketa out of a desire to see the Teacher, they were exhausted by the mud and the heat; it was there that the robe was approved for them.

Kaṭhina-v 1. The Buddha, the Blessed One, had entered the rains retreat at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery. At that time, a great number of monks who had entered the rains retreat at Sāketa, having completed the three months of the rainy season and having finished their robes, took up their bowls and robes and [set out] through the thick grass and deep mud in the heat.

Exhausted, their bodies drenched and disheveled with sweat, they traveled by way of Śrāvastī and arrived there. Then, many monks, having put away their bowls and robes and washed their feet, approached the Blessed One; having approached, they bowed their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and sat down to one side.
(Matsumura 188) Kaṭhina-v 2. It is indeed the nature of things that the Buddha-Bhagavans greet incoming monks with this greeting:
"From where, monks, have you come now?"

The Blessed One greeted the visiting monks with this greeting: "Where have you spent the rains? Have you lived in comfort? "From where do you come now, monks? Where did you spend the rains? They replied, "Venerable Sir, we [came] from Sāketa."

"We have now arrived; we spent the rains retreat at Sāketa. Did you, monks, spend the rains retreat at Sāketa in comfort? Were you not exhausted for lack of alms-food? "Truly, Venerable Sir, we spent the rains retreat at Sāketa in comfort, and we were not exhausted for lack of alms-food; however, we [spent it] having undertaken..."

Carrying their bowls and robes through fields of thick grass and deep mud, exhausted by the heat with their bodies drenched in sweat, they traveled on foot through the countryside and arrived here with great difficulty.
The Blessed One perceived this.

"Alas, my disciples are weary; having taken up their bowls and robes, they suffer in the heat amidst much grass and mud, their bodies overwhelmed by perspiration as they travel on foot through the countryside. What if I were to authorize the *kaṭhina* for the monks, for the sake of their living in comfort and for the sake of the donors' enjoyment of the gift of merit?"

Because there are five advantages to the spreading of the *kaṭhina*: [one is] not subject to the ten-day limit, nor the month-long limit, nor the requirement of staying overnight apart from one's robes; [second is] wandering through the countryside with only the inner and outer robes; and [third to fifth are] proceeding as far as necessary and wearing robes that have been formally designated (*vikalpita*).
There are also another five advantages.
There shall be no eating in groups, no eating in succession, and no wandering among families uninvited; nor shall there be the seeking of robes until one is fully satisfied.
Knowing that from the month of Kārttika until the month of Phālguna, during this interval, there is the acquisition of the spread *kaṭhina* robe-material, he addressed the monks:

Therefore, monks, I authorize that for the sake of the monks' dwelling in comfort and for the sake of the donors' enjoyment of their meritorious gifts, the kaṭhina should be spread by the monks who have completed the rains retreat. For there are five advantages in the kaṭhina: [the first being] "not beyond ten days," as previously stated, up to "the acquisition for those for whom the kaṭhina has been spread."
The Blessed One said, "The kaṭhina should be spread. The monks did not know how it should be spread.
The Blessed One said:
Whatever acquisition of robes accrues to the Saṃgha that has resided for the rains, from that the kaṭhina should be spread.

And furthermore, it should be spread in this manner as before: the assembly should be informed of its completeness, saying, "This robe-acquisition has accrued to the Saṃgha that has resided for the rains;
if it is pleasing to the Saṃgha, let the kaṭhina be made from this robe."
He shall spread it out. Thereafter, on another day, having prepared the seating and bedding,

struck the gong, and questioned the monks by means of a formal inquiry (*pṛṣṭavācikā*), when the entire Saṃgha has sat down and assembled, one monk should make a motion (*jñapti*) and perform the formal act (*karman*).

Venerable sirs, let the Saṃgha listen: this robe-material has been acquired as a robe-offering for the Saṃgha that has completed the rainy season retreat; it is the intention of the Saṃgha to spread the kaṭhina with this robe-material, so that those departing from the residence where the kaṭhina has been spread [may do so with robes].

There will be no separation even from old robes, let alone from new ones. If it seems the right time to the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha consent and authorize that the Saṃgha should formally designate this robe as the *kaṭhina* robe;
with this robe, the Saṃgha shall spread the *kaṭhina*, so that those departing from the monastery where the *kaṭhina* has been spread [will not be separated] from their old robes.
"There will be no separation [from the community], let alone for the novices"—this is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
And the formal act (karman) should be performed in this way:

"Venerable sirs, let the Saṃgha listen. This robe-material has been obtained as a gift for the Saṃgha that has spent the rains retreat, and the Saṃgha desires to make it into kaṭhina. Therefore, let the Saṃgha [accept] this robe-material for the purpose of kaṭhina."

It is resolved that with this robe the Saṅgha shall spread the *kaṭhina*; by means of which, for one departing from the residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread, there will be no separation even from old robes, let alone from new ones.
For those venerable ones who consent to approve this robe for the purpose of the *kaṭhina*, [it is resolved] that with this robe the Saṅgha...

"He who shall spread the kaṭhina—by means of which, when departing from the residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, there will be no separation even from old robes, let alone from new ones—he does not consent by remaining silent; let those who do not consent speak. This robe has been approved by the Saṃgha for the purpose of the kaṭhina; with this robe, he shall spread the kaṭhina for the Saṃgha."

"By this [formal act], when departing from the residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread, there shall be no separation even from old robes, let alone from new ones. The Saṃgha has consented and authorized it; since you are silent, I hold it to be so. (Kaṭhina-v 7) Thereafter, a monk who spreads the *kaṭhina* should be appointed by means of five qualities.
A monk who possesses these five qualities, even if he has not been appointed as the *kaṭhina*-spreader, should not be appointed; and if he has already been appointed, he should be dismissed.

What are the five? One who has not spent the rains-retreat (*avarṣika*), one whose rains-retreat was interrupted (*varṣacchinnaka*), one who entered the rains-retreat in the latter part of the season, one who spent the rains-retreat elsewhere, and one who has been granted the training (*śikṣādattaka*). Furthermore, another five should not be appointed: [the rest of the list follows].

One who is undergoing probation (*pārivāsika*), one undergoing initial probation (*mūlapārivāsika*), one undergoing a period of penance (*mānāpya*), one undergoing initial penance (*mūlamānāpya*), one who is suspended (*utkṣiptaka*), and five others should not be appointed:

one who acts out of favoritism (*chanda*), one who acts out of hatred (*dveṣa*), one who acts out of delusion (*moha*), one who acts out of fear (*bhaya*), and one who does not know whether the *kaṭhina* robe has been spread or not.
However, a monk endowed with five qualities, even if not yet appointed, should be appointed as the spreader of the *kaṭhina*.

And once he has been authorized, he must not be dismissed. By which five [qualities]? He does not act out of desire, nor out of hatred, nor out of delusion, nor out of fear; and he knows whether the *kaṭhina* has been spread or not yet spread. (*Kaṭhina-v* 8). Furthermore, he is to be authorized in this manner: having prepared the arrangement of the bedding and seats, as before (*Matsumura 198*).
He should be encouraged as follows: "Do you, [Name], have the strength to spread the *kaṭhina* for the Saṃgha? If he has the strength, he should say, "I have the strength.
Thereafter, one monk should make a formal motion (*jñapti*) and perform the ritual act (*karman*):
"Venerable sirs, let the Saṃgha listen. This monk named [Name] is the *kaṭhina*-spreader; he has the strength [to perform this duty]."

If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha should permit and authorize it, let the Saṃgha appoint such-and-such a person as the kaṭhina-spreader, so that such-and-such a kaṭhina-spreader shall spread the kaṭhina for the Saṃgha. This is the motion (*jñapti*); and the formal act (*karman*) should be performed in this manner.

"May the venerable Saṃgha listen. This one named so-and-so, the spreader of the kaṭhina, is willing to spread the kaṭhina for the Saṃgha. Therefore, let the Saṃgha appoint this one named so-and-so as the kaṭhina-spreader; this one named so-and-so, the kaṭhina-spreader, will spread the kaṭhina for the Saṃgha. To those venerable ones who approve of appointing this one named so-and-so..."

"I appoint such-and-such a person as the spreader of the *kaṭhina*; this such-and-such person shall spread the *kaṭhina* for the Saṃgha. Those who do not approve, let them speak; those who do approve, remain silent. The Saṃgha has approved such-and-such a person as the spreader of the *kaṭhina*; he shall spread the *kaṭhina* for the Saṃgha. It is accepted and authorized by the Saṃgha, since there is silence; thus do I understand this."
Kaṭhina-v 10. Thereafter, the kaṭhina should be spread by means of a formal motion (*jñapti*) from the monk who is the kaṭhina-spreader:

"Let the venerable Saṃgha listen. This robe has been approved by the Saṃgha for the purpose of the kaṭhina, and this monk named so-and-so has been approved as the kaṭhina-spreader. If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, out of compassion, grant its consent."

“That the Saṃgha should bestow this robe-cloth for the sake of the kaṭhina upon the monk named so-and-so”—this is the motion. (Kaṭhina-v 11) I shall prescribe the rules of customary conduct for the monk who spreads the kaṭhina. The monk who spreads the kaṭhina must always take precedence with the kaṭhina; whether washing it or distributing it...
While cutting, sewing, and dyeing, at the very least two or three needle-stitches must be made, and two or three thoughts [of renunciation] must be generated.
Then, afterwards, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvayuja, it should be announced: [Kaṭhina-v 12.1] (Matsumura 201)
"Venerable sirs, tomorrow I shall spread the kaṭhina;

you must each take back your own robes. Then, the monk who is the kaṭhina-spreader, having adorned the kaṭhina with perfumes and flowers and having incensed it with fragrant incense, [should perform] the arrangement of the bedding and seats.

Having struck the gong and questioned the monks through a formal inquiry, when the entire Saṃgha has assembled and is seated, it should be placed at the end of the row of elders. Then, standing at the end of the row and holding the kaṭhina-cloth, one should say:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen. This robe-cloth has been approved by the Saṃgha as the kaṭhina; I..."
"I am the monk named so-and-so, the spreader of the *kaṭhina*; as such, with this robe, I shall spread the *kaṭhina* for the Saṃgha.

Having spoken thus a second and a third time, he should then stand before the elder of the Saṃgha and say: "Pay attention, Elder; this robe has been designated as the *kaṭhina* by the Saṃgha. (Matsumura)
"I, [name], am the one who has spread the *kaṭhina*; by me, with this robe, the *kaṭhina* has been spread for the Saṃgha.

To this he should say: "It is well spread; it is properly spread; whatever gain and benefit there is herein, that is ours. Thus, twice and thrice, until the newest member of the Saṃgha, everyone should say: "Well."
"It is well spread, it is properly spread; whatever gain and benefit there is herein belongs to us," [thus says] the *Kaṭhina-v* 15.
A monk who has spread the *kaṭhina* must not, having taken up the *kaṭhina*, enter a urinal, a latrine, or a smoke-house; he must not stand in the open air, nor go outside the boundary. If...

One should not go [to that place], nor should one dwell there. If the monk who spreads the *kaṭhina* does not proceed by undertaking the rules of customary conduct as they have been prescribed, he commits an offense.
(Kaṭhina-v 16) Therefore, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Phālguna, the monk who spreads the *kaṭhina*...
Furthermore, it should be announced: "Venerable sirs, I shall suspend the *kaṭhina*; you should each consecrate your own robes.
Whatever gain has been acquired there is to be distributed by the Saṃgha.

Kaṭhina-v 17. The venerable Upāli asks the Buddha, the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, for how many is the kaṭhina not spread? "For five, Upāli: for one who has not spent the rains; for one whose rains have been interrupted; for one who has entered the rains residence during the last [month] of the rainy season; for one who has entered the rains residence elsewhere; and for one who was not present when that kaṭhina was being spread."

There are five others for whom there is no spreading [of the kaṭhina]: one who is undergoing probation (*pārivāsika*), one whose probation has been completed (*paryuṣitaparivāsa*), one who is practicing the *mānāpya* penance (*mānāpyacārika*), one who has completed the *mānāpya* penance (*caritamānāpya*), and one to whom the training has been granted (*śikṣādattaka*).
(Kaṭhina-v 18) "Venerable Sir, for how many is there gain but no benefit?"

"For five, Upāli: one who has not spent the rains, one whose rains have been cut short, one who has entered upon the later rains elsewhere, and one who has entered upon the rains [proper] but was present while the *kaṭhina* was being spread—for these five there is neither gain nor benefit.

Furthermore, for another five: one undergoing probation (*pārivāsika*), one whose probation is completed (*paryuṣitaparivāsa*), one practicing the *mānāpya*, one who has completed the *mānāpya*, and one to whom instruction has been given (*śikṣādattaka*).

For these, O Venerable One, there is indeed neither gain nor benefit. For five others, Upāli: one suspended for not seeing [an offense], one suspended for not making amends, and one suspended for not relinquishing [a wrong view]..."

[This concerns] one who has fallen into evil views, one who has been suspended (*utkṣiptaka*), one who has spent the rains elsewhere, and one who belongs to a faction in a schismatic Saṃgha regarding what is not Dharma.

(Kaṭhina-v 20) A large number of monks, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, were robbed by bandits. They eventually arrived at Śrāvastī and were seen by the resident monks, who said, "Welcome, welcome!"
"Venerable sirs, is all well with you? What is the state of your welfare? "Venerable sirs, our welfare is such that we have been robbed by thieves.
"Venerable sirs, a great gain has accrued to us; if the kaṭhina is suspended, we shall share our robes with you."
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One said:
"Therefore, I authorize that the kaṭhina should be suspended for the sake of monks who have been robbed by thieves.
Furthermore, it should be suspended in this manner: having arranged the bedding and seats, having struck the ghaṇṭī, [one should summon] the monks with a formal inquiry."
Having questioned [the monks] while the entire Saṃgha is seated and assembled, one monk should make a formal motion (*jñapti*) and perform the ritual act (*karman*).

"Listen, venerable Saṃgha! While the *kaṭhina* has been spread in this residence by the complete Saṃgha, many monks who have been robbed by thieves have arrived. If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha..."
"May the Saṃgha grant its assent and authorize that the Saṃgha shall, for the sake of those monks who have been robbed by thieves, perform the *kaṭhina*-suspension;
this is the motion (*jñapti*). And the formal act (*karman*) should be performed in this manner.
(Matsumura 207)

Venerable Saṃgha, please listen. While the kaṭhina has been spread by the entire Saṃgha in this residence, many monks who have been robbed by thieves have arrived. Therefore, the Saṃgha suspends the kaṭhina for the sake of those monks who have been robbed by thieves.
It is pleasing to those Venerable Ones [to grant] the suspension of the kaṭhina for the monks who have been robbed by thieves.

If you do not consent to the removal of the *kaṭhina* for the sake of those [monks], speak; if you remain silent, it is understood that the *saṃgha* has removed the *kaṭhina* for the sake of the monks who were robbed by thieves. Since the *saṃgha* has consented and authorized this, and because you are silent, I hold it thus. (Kaṭhina-v 22b) Therefore, whatever gain has been acquired must be distributed. Once it has been distributed, whoever so desires may, from his own allotted share, provide a portion for the monks who were robbed by thieves.
It should be performed.
The summary verse:
The fan, the writing board, the spittoon, the cloth for wiping the mouth,
the furniture for the requisites, and the old stored lungs.
Kaṭhina-v 23. The venerable Upāli asked the Buddha, the Blessed One:

"Venerable sir, is it permissible to spread the kaṭhina with a robe that has been cast away? "It is not permissible, Upāli. "Venerable sir, is it permissible [to spread the kaṭhina] with a robe that has been torn, a bathing-robe (*dakaśāṭikā*), a mouthful-robe (*gaṇḍūṣacīvara*), a strip-robe (*paṭṭikācīvara*), a patchwork-robe (*plotikācīvara*), a tiered-robe (*pariṣaṇḍācīvara*), or an old robe? [The Blessed One replied: "It is not permissible."
Upāli, it is not permitted to spread the kaṭhina with a robe that is kept nearby or a robe for the lungs.
(Matsumura 210) Summary verse: // //
If a person’s three robes have been worn out prematurely,
one should not make [new ones] that are unallowable or unwoven, nor those that are less than five [elbows].
What is not formally authorized and not spread out does not take root outside the boundary.

The Venerable Upāli asked the Buddha, the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, is it permissible to spread the kaṭhina with a garment that has been crushed? "It is not permissible, Upāli. "Venerable Sir, is it permissible to spread the kaṭhina with an out-of-season garment that is an individual saṃghāṭī? [The Buddha replied: "It is permissible, Upāli."

Upāli, it is not permitted to spread the *kaṭhina* robe with an upper garment (*uttarāsaṅga*), an inner garment (*antarvāsana*), or an improper robe; nor with a robe that is not cut, one that is less than five [cubits], or one that has not been formally authorized; nor with an unauthorized *kaṭhina*-spreader, or with a *kaṭhina* robe that has been authorized outside the boundary, or with a *kaṭhina*-spreader who has been authorized outside the boundary.
(Matsumura 213) Summary verse:
The timely robe, the three-month robe, the unhemmed robe,
the permissible robe, the emergency robe, the patched robe, and the triple-robe for an individual.

"Venerable sir, is it permissible to spread the *kaṭhina* for the Saṃgha with a robe obtained at an [inappropriate] time? "It is permissible, Upāli. "Venerable sir, is it permissible to spread the *kaṭhina* with whatever acquisition of robes accrues to the Saṃgha after the end of the three-month [rainy season]? "It is permissible, Upāli. "Is it permissible with an unwashed robe? It is permissible. Is it permissible with a robe that has been washed and prepared? It is permissible. Is it permissible with a robe obtained in an emergency? "It is permissible."

Is it permissible [to spread the kaṭhina] with a robe made of *paulotika* cloth? It is permissible. Is it permissible with a *paulotika* outer robe (*saṃghāṭī*)? It is not permissible. "Venerable Sir, is it permissible to spread the kaṭhina with an outer robe belonging to an individual? "Upāli, it is permissible if it has been relinquished to the Saṃgha. The same applies to an upper robe (*uttarāsaṅga*) and an inner robe (*antarvāsa*)."
The summary verse:
That which belongs to an individual, that which belongs to a household, the fivefold, the more-than-fivefold,
the approved, and the formally spread— these grow within the boundary.

"Venerable sir, is it permissible to spread the kaṭhina with an individual robe? "Upāli, it is not permissible. "Is it permissible if it has been relinquished to the Saṃgha? "It is permissible. "Is it permissible with a householder’s robe? "It is not permissible. "Is it permissible if it has been relinquished to the Saṃgha? "It is permissible. (Matsumura 216)

It may be obtained by means of five [measures]; it may be obtained by more than five; it may be obtained by means of a robe for the kaṭhina ceremony that has been formally approved, and by means of a kaṭhina-spreader who has been formally approved; it may be obtained by means of a robe for the kaṭhina ceremony that has been approved within the boundary, and it may be obtained by means of a kaṭhina-spreader who has been approved within the boundary.

(Kaṭhina-v 27) There are eight summary points (*mātṛkāpadas*) that lead to the suspension of the kaṭhina. Which eight? Departure, completion, final completion, loss, hearing, and crossing the boundary.

The eighth [cause for] the suspension of the *kaṭhina* is the cutting off of hope (*āśācchedaka*). The suspensions of the *kaṭhina* are: that which ends with departure (*prakramaṇāntika*), that which ends with completion (*niṣṭhāpanāntika*), that which ends with finishing (*sanniṣṭhāpanāntika*), that which ends with loss (*nāśanāntika*), that which ends with hearing (*śravaṇāntika*), that which ends with crossing the boundary (*sīmātikrāntika*), and the cutting off of hope (*āśācchedaka*)—this is indeed the eighth suspension of the *kaṭhina*.

Kaṭhina-v 28. What is the suspension of the kaṭhina by departure? It is as follows: a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither finished his robe nor completed it, takes up his bowl and robes and departs beyond the boundary with no intention of returning; for him, there is the suspension of the kaṭhina by departure.

(Matsumura 218) Kaṭhina-v 29. What is the suspension of the kaṭhina by way of completion? It is as follows: a monk, having departed from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, being without robes made and without robes finished, goes outside the boundary thinking, "I will return and make the robes."
It occurs to him: "I shall certainly not return, but rather I will make a robe. For him, there is the removal of the *kaṭhina* at the point of completion.

What is the removal of the *kaṭhina* at the point of final completion? It is as follows: a monk, from a residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread, goes outside the boundary without having made or finished a robe, thinking, "I will return and make a robe."
If it occurs to him, "I shall certainly not return, nor shall I make a robe," then his kaṭhina is suspended by way of the completion [of his intention].

Kaṭhina-v 31. What is the suspension of the kaṭhina due to loss? It is as follows: a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither finished his robe nor completed it, goes outside the boundary thinking, "I shall return and make the robe."

It occurs to him: "I shall certainly not return, but rather I will make a robe. He begins it, but what has been begun is lost. For him, there is the suspension of the *kaṭhina* at the point of its loss. (Kaṭhina-v 32) What is the suspension of the *kaṭhina* at the point of hearing? It is when a monk, from a residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread, goes outside the boundary without having made or finished a robe, thinking: "I will return and make a robe."
If the kaṭhina has been suspended by the complete Saṃgha, and he hears, "The kaṭhina has been suspended by the complete Saṃgha," and having heard it, he approves, saying, "It is well suspended;
it is properly suspended," then his suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of hearing.

(Matsumura 221) Kathina-v 33. What is the suspension of the kaṭhina due to crossing the boundary? It is as follows: a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither finished his robe nor completed it, goes outside the boundary, thinking, "I shall return" or "I shall not return."
If he crosses the boundary, his kaṭhina-suspension is due to crossing the boundary (Kaṭhina-v 34).

What is the kaṭhina-suspension for one who cuts off hope? It is as follows: a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither finished nor completed his robe, goes outside the boundary thinking, "I will return and make the robe."
Whatever expectation he has regarding robes is completely and utterly cut off; the removal of the *kaṭhina* is that which cuts off his expectation.

What is the eighth [case] of the removal of the *kaṭhina*? It is as follows: a monk who has spread the *kaṭhina* departs from his residence without having made or finished his robe, and goes beyond the boundary; upon returning, he experiences the removal of the *kaṭhina*. For him, this is the eighth removal of the *kaṭhina*.
The summary verse:
For by twenty unmade [stanzas] and twenty made,
one should compose twenty [verses] with intention, and likewise twenty without intention.

Kaṭhina-v 36. Suppose a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither made nor finished his robe, goes outside the boundary thinking, "I will return and make the robe. Then it occurs to him, "I certainly will not return, but I shall nevertheless make the robe. For him, there is the suspension of the kaṭhina at the point of completion. Kaṭhina-v 37. Suppose a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither made nor finished his robe, goes outside the boundary thinking, "I will return and make the robe."
It occurs to him: "I shall certainly not return, nor will I make a robe. For him, there is the removal of the *kaṭhina* by way of completion [of the robe].

(Kaṭhina-v 38) It is as follows: a monk, having departed from a residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread, goes outside the boundary without having made or finished a robe, thinking, "I shall return and make a robe."
He undertakes that work, but what he has undertaken perishes; for him, there is the removal of the *kaṭhina* at the point of its destruction.
(Kaṭhina-v 39) For instance, a monk who has spread the *kaṭhina* goes out from his residence—having neither finished nor completed his robe—with the thought, "I will return and make a robe.
When the *kaṭhina* has been removed by the entire Saṃgha, he hears, "The *kaṭhina* has been removed by the entire Saṃgha"; having heard this, he approves, saying, "Well removed! Thoroughly removed!"
Thus,
for him, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon hearing [the proclamation].

Kaṭhina-v 40. Suppose, for instance, that a monk who has not yet made his robe and whose robe is not yet finished departs from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, going beyond the boundary, thinking, "I will return and make the robe. While he is there, it occurs to him: "I shall certainly not return, but I will make the robe. For him, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the point of completion [of the robe]. Kaṭhina-v 41. Suppose, for instance, that a monk who has not yet made his robe and whose robe is not yet finished departs from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, going beyond the boundary, thinking, "I will return and make the robe."
When he has gone there, it occurs to him:
"I shall certainly not return, nor will I make a robe. For him, there is the removal of the *kaṭhina* at the end of its formal conclusion.

For example, suppose a monk who has not yet made or finished his robe departs from a residence where the *kaṭhina* has been spread out, intending,

Furthermore, it may happen that a monk, from a residence where the kaṭhina has been spread, having neither finished his robe nor completed his robe-making, goes outside the boundary with a mind full of attachment, thinking, "I will return and make my robe," but then it occurs to him, "I shall certainly not return; nevertheless, I will make my robe."
For him, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the conclusion of its completion.

Kaṭhina-v 56. Having removed the phrase "without having finished a robe" from the previous section of twenty cases where it says "without having made a robe and without having finished a robe," and having substituted "having interrupted the making of a robe," another set of twenty cases should be formulated in various ways.

By this specific qualification "of intention" (āśaya), another twenty-verse section is to be composed as before.
